reviewers.summary: The validator check and the added cases address the stated behavior. The unbounded regex can consume excessive CPU on a crafted long claim value.

findingList.message: The markup check can take quadratic time on untrusted values with many '<' characters and no '>'. Add a timeout or use a linear-time matching approach while preserving the required match behavior.

evidence.codePathTraced: ClaimValidator.Validate passes typedValue to MarkupLikeValuePattern.IsMatch. The unanchored pattern retries at each '<', and [^>]* scans forward to the end when the input contains no '>'.
evidence.failureScenario: A request supplies a long value such as '<a<a<a...' with no closing '>'. Each '<' can trigger another scan of the remaining string, causing quadratic work and tying up the request thread. This is a resource exhaustion risk (OWASP A06:2025, Insecure Design).

reviewers.summary: The validator applies the specified markup check after the empty-value check and before witness checks. The table-driven tests cover all 13 specified inputs, and the adversarial assessment test verifies that a matching document quote is routed to Review without creating a request. The named Test .NET CI job runs dotnet test on the solution.
The markup downgrade behavior is covered by the supplied tests, but the new unbounded regex can consume quadratic CPU on adversarial text.

findingList.message: [A06:2025] The markup check can be driven into quadratic work with an untrusted value containing many `<a` fragments and no `>`, creating a reachable denial of service.

evidence.codePathTraced: Untrusted document or model text reaches `typedValue`, which is searched by this backtracking regex without an input limit or timeout.
evidence.failureScenario: A caller supplies a long value made of repeated `<a` fragments with no closing `>`. The unanchored regex rescans the remaining suffix at each `<` before failing, consuming quadratic CPU and potentially tying up the request process.
